answer:
Ana leads it. Marco assigned it to her at Q4 planning: "the pricing page redesign ships in Q4, Ana leads it, and the target is end of September" [[M1#7]], with Ana estimating two weeks of build time once copy is approved [[M1#5]].

That end-of-September target has since slipped: legal wanted the refund section fully rewritten with a lawyer's earliest slot on the 23rd [[M2#1]], so Ana said she could be live around October 15 [[M2#3]] and Marco set that as the new target, telling the board it slipped two weeks [[M2#5]].

Northwind's invoices exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients [[M2#16]]. The cause was a rounding change made in August that only affects accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind [[M2#17]]. Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected; the calculation fix was quick, but regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the painful part [[M2#19]].

Handling: Diego fixed the calculation that day (Sept 8) and sent Northwind the list of affected invoice numbers by the next morning, with no promise of compensation, while Marco called their CFO himself [[M2#20]][[M2#21]][[M2#23]]. By the Sept 15 sync it was closed — corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and Marco had agreed to give them one month free, which Ana applied that day [[M3#9]][[M3#10]][[M3#11]].

No. The mobile app was cut from Q4 and has stayed cut.

- At Q4 planning on Sept 1, Marco decided "no mobile app in Q4," to be revisited in January if the mobile share changes [[M1#25]]. The rationale: only 8% of sessions are on a phone, mostly invoice-status checks the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], and it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[M1#24]]. Sofía added a note to the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].
- Reaffirmed Sept 8: "The mobile app is not happening... January at the earliest," within a Q4 order of pricing → checkout → SOC 2 groundwork, with nothing added unless something is removed [[M2#25]].
- At the Sept 29 retro Marco confirmed it was cut on purpose with "zero regrets," since the people asking want a feature the responsive site already provides [[M5#23]].

Note: an AI note-taker summary wrongly claimed the team decided to build the mobile app; that trial was cancelled for exactly that reason [[M3#19]][[M3#23]].

The billing address step is the main drop-off point.

- **Latest figure (Sept 15):** Sofía reported a **29% drop at the billing address step**, flat across plans and countries, after two more weeks of data [[M3#1]]. Her recommendation: remove the address step for card payments (Stripe validates the postcode itself) and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans [[M3#1]].
- **A week earlier (Sept 8)** the early data showed **28% of people who pick a plan leaving on that screen** — so the number firmed up slightly to 29% [[M2#11]].
- **Overall funnel:** on Sept 1, before instrumentation, Sofía estimated the team loses **about a third of people between picking a plan and confirming payment**, with no visibility into which step [[M1#10]]; Diego had guessed the address form because a full billing address is required even for card payments [[M1#11]]. Diego shipped the granular funnel events that Thursday [[M2#10]].

Decision: Diego and Ana build the removal, shipping one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[M3#6]][[M3#7]].

**Fifteen percent.** It was previously twenty percent, but at the September 22 design review Marco said finance wanted fifteen — "Twenty was a number I made up two years ago, and apparently it costs more than it brings in" [[M4#8]] — and he settled it: "the number is fifteen. That's a decision, I'll take the complaints" [[M4#11]].

Two related presentation decisions: the saving is shown both ways, percent on the annual toggle and the currency amount under each price [[M4#10]][[M4#11]], since Priya argued "Save 96 dollars a year" lands harder than "15 percent" [[M4#9]]. Ana was to update the mockups with the new discount by Thursday [[M4#12]].

**Drata**, decided at the September 29 retro [[M5#19]].

Why: Marco presented three quotes — Vanta, Drata, and Secureframe — all within twenty percent of each other on price. Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of the team's evidence collection; Vanta only had a nicer dashboard, and Secureframe was cheapest but had a smaller auditor network [[M5#16]]. Diego, who has to feed the platform, said integrations matter more than the dashboard [[M5#17]], and Sofía agreed [[M5#18]].

Note the shortlist widened along the way: in the September 1 planning meeting the evaluation was limited to Vanta and Drata [[M1#22]]; Secureframe was added by the time quotes were presented [[M5#16]].

Next steps: Marco signs the contract in the first week of October, and Diego kicks off the integrations after the checkout change ships, so late October [[M5#19]]. The audit itself is Q1 — evidence collection takes three months minimum — and Marco will tell Northwind that timeline [[M5#22]].
unsupported_claims: in the September 1 planning meeting the evaluation was limited to Vanta and Drata

The September 1 Q4 planning meeting (Marco, Ana, Sofía, Diego) settled four items:

Sofía had no bandwidth, so it stayed on the list without an owner, to be revisited the following week; Diego was told to add the funnel events anyway, by Friday [[M1#16]][[M1#17]]. (Diego's hunch: the billing address form, which Stripe doesn't need for card payments [[M1#11]].)

**SOC 2** — Driven by two customer requests in August, one of them Northwind, the biggest account [[M1#18]]. Marco took the action to get vendor quotes and bring them to the end-of-month retro [[M1#20]], narrowed to Vanta and Drata [[M1#21]][[M1#22]].

**Mobile app** — Not happening in Q4; revisit in January if the mobile session share changes [[M1#25]]. Rationale: only 8% of sessions are on a phone, mostly invoice checks the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], and it would consume the quarter for two people [[M1#24]]. Sofía to update the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].

**Also:** Diego to upgrade the staging Postgres version next week, ahead of the pricing launch [[M1#30]][[M1#31]].

**Scope and ownership (Sept 1)** — The redesign ships in Q4, Ana leads, three tiers instead of five, an annual billing toggle, and the comparison table moved below the fold [[M1#3]][[M1#7]]. Original target: live by end of September, which Ana flagged as a target, not a promise, dependent on legal signing off the refund wording [[M1#5]][[M1#8]].

**Sequencing** — Pricing launches before the checkout work starts, so the two changes can be measured separately [[M1#6]][[M1#7]]. This held: on Sept 8 Marco reaffirmed no overlap [[M2#5]], and on Sept 15 the billing-address removal was set to ship one week *after* pricing goes live, ~Oct 22 [[M3#5]][[M3#6]]. Diego's production Postgres upgrade was also pushed to the week after pricing launches [[M2#8]].

**Date change (Sept 8)** — End of September was dropped. Legal wanted the refund section fully rewritten by a lawyer whose earliest slot was the 23rd, so the new target is **October 15**; Marco took the action of telling the board it slipped two weeks and why [[M2#1]][[M2#3]][[M2#5]]. Ana reconfirmed Oct 15 on Sept 15 [[M3#13]] and again on Sept 22 [[M4#26]][[M4#27]].

**Design review decisions (Sept 22, with Priya)**
- Emphasize the middle tier: stronger border, filled instead of outlined button, offset upward so it breaks the line [[M4#3]][[M4#6]].
- Annual discount drops from 20% to **15%** (finance's call); Marco owned the decision [[M4#6]][[M4#11]].
- Show the saving both ways: percent on the toggle, currency amount under each price [[M4#9]][[M4#10]][[M4#11]].
- Comparison table stays below the fold, with anchor links from each tier to its column [[M4#16]][[M4#17]].
- No fourth enterprise tier — instead one line under the table: "Need more than fifty seats? Talk to us." [[M4#21]][[M4#22]].
- Free tier shows "0 dollars" in the same position as the other prices [[M4#24]][[M4#25]].
- Supporting actions: Ana updates mockups by Thursday, Priya sends a consistent icon set by Wednesday [[M4#12]][[M4#13]].

**Retro assessment (Sept 29)** — Marco judged the slip the right call: waiting rather than building the page twice was correct even though it cost two weeks, and the lesson is to stop planning around dates other people control [[M5#23]]; Ana named the same mistake [[M5#5]].

Ana flagged it as "target, not promise" if legal was slow [[M1#8]].
- **Now:** October 15. On Sept 8 Ana reported legal wanted the refund section fully rewritten, with the lawyer's earliest slot on the 23rd [[M2#1]], so "end of September is gone" [[M2#2]] and she could be live "around the fifteenth of October" [[M2#3]]. Marco set the new target and said he'd tell the board it slipped two weeks [[M2#5]].

It has held since: on Sept 15 Ana said "I'm still saying October fifteenth" [[M3#13]], and at the Sept 22 design review Marco and Ana confirmed "we're still on for the fifteenth" [[M4#26]][[M4#27]]. At the Sept 29 retro Marco characterized the slip as the correct call — waiting rather than building the page twice, at a cost of two weeks [[M5#23]].

Knock-on effects: the checkout billing-address change ships one week after pricing, around October 22 [[M3#6]][[M3#7]], and the production Postgres upgrade waits until the week after pricing launches [[M2#8]].

On September 1, Marco asked who owned checkout abandonment [[M1#13]]. Sofía said someone should look at it properly with instrumentation rather than guesses, but she lacked bandwidth that month because of the pricing analysis [[M1#14]]; Diego offered to add the funnel events (a day of work) but not the analysis [[M1#15]]. Marco left it on the list with no owner, to revisit the next week, while telling Diego to add the events anyway [[M1#16]] — Diego committed to Friday [[M1#17]].

With the pricing analysis mostly done and the data now visible, Sofía volunteered to own the checkout work [[M2#13]], and Marco confirmed her as owner [[M2#14]]. Her next step: a proposal by the following Monday with the data and a recommendation, probably removing the address step for card payments [[M2#15]].

Sofía raised the mobile app in Q4 planning but argued against it herself: support keeps getting asked for it, but only eight percent of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]]. After Marco decided against it, she offered to put a note in the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]].

The following week, when Marco restated that the mobile app is not happening and January is the earliest [[M2#25]], Sofía asked him to put the roadmap statement in writing so she could link it from the support macro [[M2#26]].

answer:
Three items were raised with no owner; two later got one.

**1. Checkout abandonment analysis (M1, Sept 1) — later owned by Sofía.**
Sofía said she lacked bandwidth, Diego could add funnel events but not do the analysis [[M1#14]][[M1#15]], so Marco left it "on the list without an owner for now" and asked Diego to instrument anyway [[M1#16]]. One week later, with data showing a 28% drop at the billing address step, Sofía volunteered and Marco confirmed: "Sofía owns checkout abandonment" [[M2#13]][[M2#14]], with a proposal due the following Monday [[M2#15]]. It converted into a real decision on Sept 15 — remove the address step for card payments, built by Diego and Ana, shipping ~Oct 22 [[M3#6]][[M3#7]].

**2. Written deploy process (M5, Sept 29) — later owned by Diego.**
Diego raised it as something that didn't go well; Sofía's "Somebody should really write that down" got Diego's "Yes. Somebody," and Marco deferred it [[M5#6]][[M5#7]][[M5#8]]. It was picked back up at the end of the same retro: Marco assigned it to Diego, not that week, and Diego committed to mid-October, after the checkout change [[M5#26]][[M5#27]][[M5#28]][[M5#29]].

**3. The refund copy for the pricing page — never owned inside the team.**
It was flagged as the open item on Sept 1: Carla from legal still had to sign off on the refund wording [[M1#3]]. It stayed outside the team's control — legal wanted a full rewrite by a lawyer whose earliest slot was the 23rd [[M2#1]], which pushed the pricing launch to Oct 15 [[M2#3]][[M2#5]]. At the Sept 22 design review it was still the one missing piece, "which legal sends tomorrow" [[M4#0]]. Marco's retro takeaway was exactly this: stop planning around dates other people control [[M5#23]].

Related: at the retro Marco also removed himself as owner of procurement work, since he sat on the SOC 2 quotes for a month [[M5#23]] — no replacement owner was named, though he kept the Drata signature himself [[M5#19]].

answer: At the September 22 design review, Marco asked whether the pricing page should have an enterprise "contact us" tier, since sales kept raising it [[M4#18]]. Priya first asked whether they actually sell enterprise; Marco said two accounts, one of them Northwind [[M4#19]][[M4#20]]. Her recommendation: no fourth tier — instead a single line under the comparison table reading "Need more than fifty seats? Talk to us," because a fourth tier makes the three look smaller [[M4#21]]. Marco agreed on the spot ("One line, no fourth tier") and Ana added it [[M4#22]][[M4#23]].

Carla never speaks in any of these meetings — she isn't a participant. She's only mentioned by Ana as the legal contact: on September 1 Ana said "Carla from legal still has to sign off on the refund wording" [[M1#3]], and on September 8 Ana reported that legal wanted the refund section rewritten rather than tweaked, with "Carla wants a lawyer to draft it, and their earliest slot is the twenty-third" [[M2#1]].

Marco's Q4 order: **pricing page first, then checkout, then SOC 2 groundwork** — "in that order, and nothing gets added unless something gets removed" [[M2#25]]. The mobile app is explicitly out (January at the earliest) [[M2#25]].

Why the order matters, in his words: "each of these changes the numbers the next one depends on. If we launch checkout changes in the same week as pricing, we won't know which one moved conversion, and we'll spend November arguing about it instead of shipping. So: one thing at a time, measured, then the next" [[M2#25]]. Sofía made the same attribution argument at Q4 planning — launch pricing before starting checkout work, "otherwise I can't tell which change moved the numbers" — and Marco agreed [[M1#6]][[M1#7]].

How it played out in scheduling:
- Pricing slipped from end of September to **October 15** because of the legal refund copy, and Marco chose to let that push checkout rather than overlap: "Let's not overlap them" [[M2#3]][[M2#5]].
- The checkout change (removing the billing address step for card payments) is built now but ships **one week after pricing goes live**, around October 22 — Sofía's framing was "ship it after pricing is live and has a week of data" [[M3#5]][[M3#6]][[M3#7]].
- Even the production Postgres upgrade was sequenced behind the launch: Diego does it "the week after pricing launches, not before" [[M2#8]].
unsupported_claims: Pricing slipped from end of September to October 15 'because of the legal refund copy' — the cited line only mentions waiting for unspecified copy, not that it was legal/refund copy.
